findings.what: Live dispatch treats most deriveBinding ok:false results as advisory instead of refusing the spawn.
findings.why: deriveBinding's contract says ok:false means the dispatch must be refused, but both wrappers only exit when the reason matches President-leak/top_level_session-only/category error. Corrupt or unreadable role-binding.json, ED-220 value-invalid graphs, unknown roles, and other unbound states continue toward spawn with only WARPOS_ACTOR_KIND stamped. That violates the required fail-closed behavior for trusted binding-control failures.

findings.what: Known-role validation fails open when the role registry cannot be read.
findings.why: defaultKnownRoles catches registry failures and returns [], and deriveBinding only rejects unknown roles when knownRoles.length is truthy. With that empty set, arbitrary non-hardcoded roles bind ok:true through validated_workorder_or_cli, including President-like aliases such as alex_alpha/alexAlpha/president-worker. Missing-role validation must fail closed, not disappear under registry failure.

findings.what: The resolver takes its binding-control root from CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR instead of the dispatch script's canonical root.
findings.why: defaultKernelDir follows process.env.CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR, while dispatch-contract hard-anchors registry identity to __dirname to avoid hostile or stale env-root influence. A stale or attacker-controlled environment can make deriveBinding consult a different .claude/kernel/role-binding.json; combined with the wrapper advisory path, that becomes a live fail-open route.

parsed.summary: FAIL. The channel-derived design is present, category-error President roles are refused, and gauntlet signature verification rejects forged unsigned ok:true records when requireSignature is enabled. The binding is not enforceable yet because live dispatch does not refuse all resolver failures and the resolver disables unknown-role validation on registry failure.
